- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes, especially after bullish sentiment events or high supply net events — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such contexts.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — apply a “lag correction” by holding forecast at previous peak for 2–3 periods before resuming trend.
- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and supply net is negative, model underreacts — increase forecast baseline by 3–7% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model overreacts — reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid overcorrection.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if price deviates >10% from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward average with decay factor of 0.8 per period.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true volatility — add 1–3% volatility buffer to forecast if recent sentiment or supply events are volatile or clustered.
